narrationDirection: Perform this original Thai romantic comedy as a native Bangkok Thai man telling a friend an embarrassing true story, half laughing at himself. Same warm male narrator as Part 1. Brisk, connected conversational phrasing with varied stress; never the same rise and fall on each phrase. Open firm and a little nervous: he has decided to tell the truth. The false starts are dry and funny. The lobby lines lean in conspiratorially. The cafe memory is sincere and quiet, the confession a little ashamed, never melodramatic. When the phone rings, a quick jolt, then a stunned beat on the name. The lobby gasp is a comedy peak. The final question is direct to the viewer. Natural thought-group breaths, no long gaps. Read only the provided Thai text; do not speak these instructions or bracketed delivery tags.
